title: Billed generations that failed after a 200 released their budget
body:
## Summary
generateTts/generateMusic released the budget reservation on ANY error, including a 200 whose body was then rejected and a network failure after the request left - work the provider billed (or may have).

## Description
packages/audio/src/budget.ts:74 documents `release` as "the provider produced nothing billable", but packages/audio/src/generate.ts (both produce callbacks) called `deps.budget.release(r)` in every catch. A TTS 200 without alignment (packages/audio/src/client.ts:303), an empty music body (packages/audio/src/client.ts composeMusic) and a socket failure all vanished from the per-run DESIGN 6.4 budget. Registry: software-engineering/cost-metering "Failures are spend" and reversible-debit-and-settle. Fixed: `settleOrRelease` releases only on a provider error status (ProviderError httpStatus >= 400) and settles everything else at the reserved estimate (fail closed).

## Flow
- live audio job -> ElevenLabs answers 200 with alignment null -> ttsWithTimestamps throws ProviderError(200)
- generate.ts catch -> budget.release -> budget.used('tts') back to 0, generations not counted
- fix: settleOrRelease(budget, r, e) - release only when e is ProviderError with httpStatus >= 400

## Expected impact
The per-run budget now counts what ElevenLabs billed; a run that hits malformed responses refuses earlier instead of overspending. Could break: a run with transient network failures now uses up budget it may not have spent (conservative by design).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the spend ceiling counts billed failures
Before: 200-without-alignment TTS -> 0 s charged; 200-empty music -> 0 s; network failure -> 0 s (3 generate.test cases seeded red)
After: 4 s / 8 s / 4 s charged; a 4xx refusal still releases
Method: gate - red-then-green generate.test cases on the real change
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
packages/audio/src/budget.ts:74 `/** Give the reservation back (the provider produced nothing billable). */`
packages/audio/src/generate.ts (pre-fix) `} catch (e) { deps.budget.release(r); throw e; }` x2
generate.test red: "expected +0 to be 4" / "expected +0 to be 8"

title: ElevenLabs requests had no timeout and the job's cancel could not reach them
body:
## Summary
ElevenLabsClient called fetch with no signal and no timeout, so a silent provider hung the audio job and a cancel could not stop an in-flight generation.

## Description
packages/audio/src/client.ts send() passed `{ method, headers, body }` to fetch with no AbortSignal; apps/server/src/pipeline.ts:169 constructs the client per audio job but could not hand it ctx.signal. DESIGN 6.3 (robustness 2026-10-04) says "cancel reaches audio". Registry: retry-backoff/error-classification-for-retry (a timed-out write that may have landed is not retried). Fixed: `timeoutMs` (default 300000 per attempt, body included) and `signal` options; a timeout is ProviderError code "timeout" (not retried; since ce30fbd its reservation stays charged); a cancel rejects with the signal's reason; a pre-aborted client never reaches the provider.

## Flow
- provider accepts the connection and goes silent -> await fetch never settles -> audio job runs until the process dies
- owner cancels -> ctx.signal aborts -> the pending fetch ignores it
- fix: AbortSignal.any([caller signal, AbortSignal.timeout(timeoutMs)]) on every attempt; map timeout vs cancel

## Expected impact
An unattended produce run fails in at most 5 min per call instead of hanging; cancel stops a generation once the pipeline passes its signal (Lane B card). Could break: a music call that legitimately takes > 300 s now fails (well above the 75 s budget's generation time).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - no audio job hangs on a silent provider
Before: hanging fetch -> request still pending after 1 s; abort -> still pending (2 client.test cases seeded red)
After: ProviderError "timed out after 20 ms"; abort -> rejects with the caller's reason; pre-aborted -> fetch never called
Method: gate - red-then-green client.test cases with a fetch that only settles on abort
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
packages/audio/src/client.ts (pre-fix) `res = await this.fetchImpl(url, body === undefined ? { method: req.method, headers } : { method: req.method, headers, body })`
apps/server/src/pipeline.ts:169 `new ElevenLabsClient({ apiKey: async () => secret("elevenlabs") })` (no signal)
client.test red: "expected 'still hanging after 1 s' to be an instance of ProviderError"

title: Assets stamped today's plan tier, even on takes generated under an older plan
body:
## Summary
generateTts/generateMusic stamped the run's subscription tier on every asset, cache hits included, and the cache record kept no tier - a free-plan take served after an upgrade read as commercially cleared.

## Description
packages/audio/src/generate.ts set `if (deps.planTier) asset.plan_tier = deps.planTier` for every entry source; packages/audio/src/cache.ts CacheMeta had no plan tier. Registry: media-generation/generated-music-acceptance rights-and-provenance-record - "vendor commercial grants are plan-scoped and non-retroactive"; DESIGN 6.4 "record plan tier per asset". Fixed: the cache record stores `plan_tier` at generation (Produced.planTier -> CacheMeta.plan_tier) and the asset takes it from the record; a legacy entry carries none (the publish gate denies it).

## Flow
- free plan: generate a TTS line -> cached
- upgrade to creator -> rerun -> cache hit -> asset.plan_tier 'creator'
- fix: generatedPlanTier(entry) reads meta.plan_tier; absent -> no plan_tier

## Expected impact
The rights record says what the take was generated under, so the publish gate cannot clear a free-plan take. Could break: replay fixtures recorded before this carry no tier on the asset (the pipeline still writes its own tier to the DB - Lane B card).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the asset's plan tier is the generation-time tier
Before: free-plan take, cache hit under 'creator' -> 'creator'; legacy entry -> today's tier (2 generate.test cases seeded red)
After: 'free' / absent
Method: gate - red-then-green generate.test cases
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
packages/audio/src/generate.ts (pre-fix) `if (deps.planTier) asset.plan_tier = deps.planTier;` (tts + music)
packages/audio/src/cache.ts CacheMeta (pre-fix): key, kind, request, alignment, normalized_alignment, request_id, model, generated_at, sha256, bytes - no tier
generate.test red: "expected undefined to be 'free'"

title: Bed envelope sagged into the Powered duck across the spotlight and like cards
body:
## Summary
planBedFromTimingPlan's level() holds 0 dB until the Powered card, but the envelope had no breakpoint before the duck, so bedLevelDbAt ramped from the spotlight lift's end and the bed sagged for ~2.6 s.

## Description
packages/audio/src/bed.ts breaks were {0, musicEnd, poweredStart, lift points}; bedLevelDbAt (packages/audio/src/bed.ts) interpolates linearly between consecutive breakpoints, so between the spotlight lift end (39.4 s) and the card (42 s) it returned -0.12 ... -2.99 dB while level() says 0. Registry: media-generation/video-assembly music-spotting-against-picture (sound leads picture). Fixed: an attack breakpoint at poweredStart - eventLeadS (0.15 s), the same lead the lifts use.

## Flow
- 45 s plan -> planBedFromTimingPlan -> envelope [.., 39.4: 0, 42: -3, ..]
- bedLevelDbAt(41) -> -1.85 dB under the like card
- fix: add r6(poweredStart - lead) to breaks

## Expected impact
When the AudioTracks consumer lands (vault open item), the bed holds level through the spotlight and like cards and ducks just ahead of the Powered card. No product consumer today.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the evaluated envelope matches the planner's level rule
Before: 39.5 s -0.12, 40 s -0.69, 41 s -1.85, 41.99 s -2.99 dB where level() = 0 (probe; bed.test seeded red)
After: 0 dB from 39.4 to 41.85 s, -1.5 at 41.925 s, -3 at 42 s
Method: gate - red-then-green bed.test sweep over the gap
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
packages/audio/src/bed.ts (pre-fix) `const breaks = new Set<number>([0, musicEnd, poweredStart]);`
probe envelope: [{37.85,0},{38,2},{38.8,2},{39.4,0},{42,-3},{44.5,-3}]; bedLevelDbAt(41) = -1.846

title: Bed loop crossfade as long as the take hung the planner forever
body:
## Summary
planBedFromTimingPlan's loop branch divided by (take - crossfade) with no check: crossfadeS equal to the take made n = Infinity and the loop pushed cues until the process died.

## Description
packages/audio/src/bed.ts loop branch: `n = Math.max(2, Math.ceil((musicEnd - xf) / (l0 - xf)))` then `for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) cues.push(...)`. crossfadeS 30 with the 30 s take -> Infinity; a negative crossfade left 1 s holes while coverage reported them scored; loopS NaN planned 0 cues and a NaN-length take. The planner already throws RangeError for fps, budget and section order. Fixed: loopS > 0 and 0 <= crossfadeS < take, RangeError otherwise.

## Flow
- planBedFromTimingPlan(90 s plan, { budgetS: 75, crossfadeS: 30 }) -> never returns
- fix: validate loop options inside the loop branch before computing n

## Expected impact
A bad option fails fast with its name instead of hanging the server process; defaults and the smallest legal budget plan as before.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - no input hangs the bed planner
Before: crossfadeS 30 -> killed by `timeout 8` (exit 124); crossfadeS -1 -> 3 cues with 1 s gaps; loopS NaN -> 0 cues, lengthMs null (bed.test seeded red)
After: RangeError naming the option in all three
Method: gate - bed.test red-then-green (the hang case proven by a timed probe, not run red in vitest)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
packages/audio/src/bed.ts (pre-fix) `const n = Math.max(2, Math.ceil((musicEnd - xf) / (l0 - xf)));`
probe: `timeout 8 tsx probe2.ts 30` -> exit=124

title: A NaN budget limit silently allowed unlimited ElevenLabs spend
body:
## Summary
Budget compared `used + s > limit`; a NaN limit makes every comparison false, so reserve() never refused.

## Description
packages/audio/src/budget.ts constructor took `opts.ttsSeconds ?? 75` unchecked; reserve() at packages/audio/src/budget.ts:58 refuses only when the comparison is true. Number("75s") from a setting turns the per-run DESIGN 6.4 ceiling off. Registry: cost-metering/budget-enforcement (fail-open vs fail-closed; the unlimited sentinel is explicit). Fixed: each limit must be a finite number >= 0 at construction.

## Flow
- new Budget({ musicSeconds: Number('75s') }).reserve('music', 600) -> succeeds
- fix: constructor throws RangeError

## Expected impact
A misconfigured limit stops the job instead of spending without a ceiling. Only in-tree caller passes 75/75.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the spend ceiling fails closed
Before: "reserved 600 s against limit NaN" (probe; budget.test seeded red)
After: RangeError "music budget must be a finite number of seconds >= 0, got NaN"
Method: gate - red-then-green budget.test
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
packages/audio/src/budget.ts:58 (pre-fix) `if (this.usedS[kind] + seconds > this.limits[kind] + EPS)` with limits unchecked
probe: reserved 600 s against limit NaN

title: A truncated cache or fixture record failed with a bare JSON error, no path
body:
## Summary
AudioCache.read parsed the metadata with a bare JSON.parse, so a truncated or null record surfaced as SyntaxError/TypeError with no file and no remedy.

## Description
packages/audio/src/cache.ts read(): `JSON.parse(readFileSync(metaPath))` then `meta.sha256`. The sibling failure (sha mismatch) already raises CacheCorrupt naming the path with "delete both and regenerate". An interrupted AUDIO_RECORD copy (copyToFixtures is non-atomic - Lane B card) leaves exactly this shape in e2e/fixtures/audio, the paid fixtures. Fixed: unreadable or sha-less records raise CacheCorrupt with the record path and the same remedy.

## Flow
- replay e2e reads a truncated fixture .json -> 'SyntaxError: Unterminated string in JSON' fails the audio job
- fix: try/catch + shape check -> CacheCorrupt

## Expected impact
The operator sees which fixture is broken and what to do, instead of a JSON parser message.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the failure names its file and remedy
Before: '{"key":"' -> SyntaxError, 'null' -> TypeError, '' -> SyntaxError (cache.test seeded red)
After: CacheCorrupt '<path>.json: unreadable record (...); delete both and regenerate'
Method: gate - red-then-green cache.test
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
packages/audio/src/cache.ts (pre-fix) `const meta = JSON.parse(readFileSync(metaPath, "utf8")) as CacheMeta;`
cache.test red: "expected SyntaxError: Unterminated string in JSON ... to be an instance of CacheCorrupt"

title: Billed 200s with an unusable body dropped the provider request-id
body:
## Summary
composeMusic (empty body) and forcedAlignment (no characters/words) raised ProviderError without the response's request-id, while ttsWithTimestamps carries it.

## Description
packages/audio/src/client.ts composeMusic read `request-id` only after the empty-body check; forcedAlignment never read it. Those failures are billed (ce30fbd keeps their budget) and the request-id is what an ElevenLabs support/refund claim needs. Fixed: both errors carry requestId.

## Flow
- music compose 200 with 0 bytes + request-id m-9 -> err.requestId undefined
- fix: read the header before the check and pass it to ProviderError

## Expected impact
The operator can quote the request in a support claim for a billed empty take.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every post-200 ProviderError carries the request-id (3 of 3)
Before: 1 of 3 (client.test seeded red: "expected undefined to be 'm-9'")
After: 3 of 3
Method: gate - red-then-green client.test
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: packages/audio/src/client.ts (pre-fix) composeMusic: `if (audio.length === 0) throw new ProviderError(..., { httpStatus: res.status });` before `const requestId = res.headers.get("request-id")`

title: Six of eight pre-call music rejections bypassed InvalidMusicRequest
body:
## Summary
buildMusicRequest typed only its two section checks as InvalidMusicRequest; the length limit, instrumental flag, prompt/plan exclusivity, empty prompt, section sum and lyrics threw bare Error/RangeError.

## Description
packages/audio/src/errors.ts InvalidMusicRequest is "a music request the API would reject, caught before any paid call" with `field`, `fix` and "No ElevenLabs call was made." packages/audio/src/client.ts buildMusicRequest used it at 2 sites (64982ae) and plain errors at 6, one of them a documented API limit (3000-600000 ms). Fixed: all 8 use it with the field path; the RangeError test is strengthened to pin the new type.

## Flow
- generateMusic with musicLengthMs 2999 -> RangeError without field or 'no call made'
- fix: InvalidMusicRequest(field, fix) at every pre-call check

## Expected impact
One error shape for every request we refuse before paying; job status unchanged ('failed').

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one rule, one implementation
Before: 2 of 8 pre-call rejection sites typed (client.test seeded red)
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - red-then-green client.test over all six shapes
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: packages/audio/src/client.ts (pre-fix) :118 `throw new RangeError(...)`, :119/:124/:137/:139/:151 `throw new Error(...)`; :129/:134 `throw new InvalidMusicRequest(...)`

title: An empty TTS alignment for real text passed as a 0 s voice
body:
## Summary
isAlignment accepted three empty arrays, so a 200 with no aligned characters for non-empty text succeeded with durationS 0.

## Description
packages/audio/src/client.ts isAlignment checks only array-ness and equal lengths. generateTts then settled the budget at 0 s, the pipeline laid the next scene at the same cursor and the scene got no caption words. Registry: software-engineering/voice-io render-acceptance ("a synthesis call returns successfully and the audio is garbage"). Fixed: an empty alignment for non-empty text is the same ProviderError as a missing one.

## Flow
- TTS 200 with alignment {characters: []} for 'Hello there.' -> resolved
- fix: reject when characters is empty and text.trim() is not

## Expected impact
Garbage TTS output fails visibly (and stays charged) instead of producing an uncaptioned zero-length scene.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - degenerate TTS output is a failure, not a success
Before: resolved {audio, alignment} (client.test seeded red)
After: ProviderError "returned no character alignment"
Method: gate - red-then-green client.test
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Loudness ffmpeg runs could not receive the job's cancel signal
body:
## Summary
measureLoudness, normalizeTo and probeDurationS spawned ffmpeg/ffprobe with no signal option, while the render job passes its signal to every ffmpeg it spawns itself.

## Description
packages/audio/src/loudness.ts run() called execFile without a signal; apps/server/src/pipeline.ts:296-308 pass `{ signal }` to their own execFileP calls but `normalizeTo` (2 ffmpeg passes, an ffprobe, a re-measure) and `measureLoudness` could not take one. DESIGN 6.3: "cancel reaches audio, ffmpeg and the worker process tree". Fixed: CancelOptions `{ signal }` on all three; pre-aborted spawns nothing; mid-run abort kills the child; rejection carries the signal's reason.

## Flow
- owner cancels during mastering -> normalizeTo runs both passes to completion
- fix: execFile({ signal }) and reject with signal.reason

## Expected impact
Cancel stops mastering once the pipeline passes the signal (Lane B card).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - cancel reaches the loudness children
Before: normalizeTo with a signal aborted after 20 ms resolved with its loudness (loudness.test seeded red)
After: rejects with the caller's reason; pre-aborted calls never spawn
Method: gate - red-then-green loudness.test with real ffmpeg
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
packages/audio/src/loudness.ts (pre-fix) `execFile(bin, args, { maxBuffer: 64 * 1024 * 1024, windowsHide: true }, ...)`
apps/server/src/pipeline.ts:297 `await normalizeTo({ input: mixWav, output: masterWav, targetLufs: -14, truePeak: -2.3 });` beside :296 `execFileP("ffmpeg", [...], { signal })`

instrument: pipeline.test: audio job with a fetch that settles only on abort; abort ctx -> job status 'cancelled' within 1 s (red today)
title: Pipeline does not hand the job's cancel signal to the audio client or loudness
body:
## Summary
The audio and render jobs construct ElevenLabsClient and call normalizeTo/measureLoudness without ctx.signal, so the cancel support added in d7fe97c and 920ec25 is not wired.

## Description
apps/server/src/pipeline.ts:169 `new ElevenLabsClient({ apiKey })` and :297/:303 `normalizeTo({...})`, `measureLoudness(video)` take no signal; cancel only lands between generations (`stop()` at :161). Out of this context's paths (Projects & Produce Pipeline).

## Flow
- pass `signal: ctx.signal` to the client constructor
- pass `signal` to normalizeTo and measureLoudness in renderRun
- pipeline.test: hanging fetch + abort -> job ends cancelled within 1 s

## Expected impact
Cancel during a generation or mastering returns in milliseconds instead of after the call finishes.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - cancel reaches in-flight audio work
Before: aborting ctx.signal during a hanging generation leaves the job pending (walked: pipeline.ts:169 has no signal)
After: predicted rejection with the cancel reason; falsified if the runner records 'failed' instead of 'cancelled'
Method: simulation - three call sites read in pipeline.ts; out-of-scope file, no edit this round
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: apps/server/src/pipeline.ts:169, :297, :303 (no signal); packages/audio/src/client.ts ElevenLabsClientOptions.signal; packages/audio/src/loudness.ts CancelOptions

instrument: pipeline.test seeding a cache record with plan_tier 'free' under planTier 'starter' -> inserted row plan_tier (red today: 'starter')
title: Pipeline writes the run's plan tier to asset rows instead of the asset's own
body:
## Summary
The audio job inserts `plan_tier: planTier ?? null` (the run's subscription) for every asset, ignoring the generation-time tier generate.ts now records (92e1f6b).

## Description
apps/server/src/pipeline.ts:234 (`plan_tier: planTier ?? null`) - the DB row and manifest.audio the publish gate reads still carry today's tier for cache hits. Registry: rights-and-provenance-record (non-retroactive grants). Caveat: replay fixtures recorded before 92e1f6b carry no tier, so a replay run would need e2e/fixtures/audio/plan-tier.json as the explicit replay source (a decision the worker records), and no fixture may be re-recorded (paid).

## Flow
- insert `plan_tier: a.plan_tier ?? null`
- replay mode: fall back to plan-tier.json only for source 'fixture'
- pipeline.test: cache hit recorded 'free' under a 'starter' run -> row 'free'

## Expected impact
A free-plan take reused after an upgrade can no longer pass the publish gate. Could break: replay e2e manifest check (m1.spec.ts:87) if the fallback is wrong.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - DB asset rows carry the generation-time tier
Before: row tier = run tier for every asset (read: pipeline.ts insert)
After: predicted row = recorded tier; falsified if m1.spec plan_tier check fails in replay
Method: simulation - insert site read; out-of-scope file
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: apps/server/src/pipeline.ts:234 `plan_tier: planTier ?? null`; e2e/m1.spec.ts:87 `x.plan_tier && x.plan_tier !== "free"`; e2e/fixtures/audio/plan-tier.json

instrument: mix.test: for a cue with no overlapping voice, volumeDbAt(envelope, mid) === timelineMusic gain_db (red today: -3 vs -6)
title: mixPlan plays a voiceless bed at the open level, 3 dB over its declared gain
body:
## Summary
For bed cues with no voice, mixPlan's envelope holds musicOpenDb (-3 dB) while its own timelineMusic says gain_db -6, the bed's declared level.

## Description
packages/audio/src/mix.ts builds envelope points as `open + (duck - open) * ducked(t)`; with scenes [] ducked is 0, so -3. timelineMusic uses `c.gainDb` (-6). MusicCue.gainDb means 'level under voice' for planMusicCues (packages/audio/src/music.ts) but 'the bed level' for planBedFromTimingPlan (packages/audio/src/bed.ts BedOptions.gainDb). Coupled to the open AudioTracks consumer change (vault audio-bed-from-timing-plan build record) - whichever output the consumer plays decides the bed's loudness.

## Flow
- planBed(45 s) -> attachBedSources -> mixPlan({ scenes: [], cues })
- volumeDbAt(envelope, 10) = -3 vs timelineMusic gain_db = -6
- decide: a voiceless track holds its cue gain, or the bed passes musicOpenDb = gainDb

## Expected impact
The bed plays at one level whichever mixPlan output the renderer adopts.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one mix level per cue
Before: 3 dB disagreement (probe)
After: 0 dB disagreement under either fix; the choice of level is the worker's to justify
Method: probe - planBed + mixPlan on a 45 s plan; not built because the semantics of gainDb split between two planners and the consumer is unbuilt
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
probe4: envelope dB at 10 s: -3, timelineMusic gain_db: -6, bed gainDb: -6
packages/audio/src/bed.ts header: "mixPlan only ducks under voice; with no scenes it holds the open level"

instrument: cache.test with fs.copyFileSync mocked to throw after writing half the bytes -> no <key>.json in fixturesDir (red today)
title: Recording copies fixtures non-atomically into the paid fixture set
body:
## Summary
AudioCache.copyToFixtures copies the mp3 then the json with plain copyFileSync, so an interrupted AUDIO_RECORD run can leave a truncated fixture record in e2e/fixtures/audio.

## Description
packages/audio/src/cache.ts copyToFixtures uses copyFileSync twice, while the cache's own writes go through atomicWrite (tmp + rename). Fixtures are paid and gitignored; a truncated one now fails as CacheCorrupt (b44ac52) but is still lost and can only be replaced by a paid re-record.

## Flow
- live run with AUDIO_RECORD=1 killed during copyFileSync(meta)
- fixture .json truncated -> replay e2e CacheCorrupt
- fix: copy to `<dst>.<pid>.tmp` then rename, meta last

## Expected impact
A killed recording run cannot corrupt a paid fixture. Could break: nothing visible on the success path.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - fixture writes are all-or-nothing
Before: 2 non-atomic copies per recorded entry (read)
After: predicted 0 partial files under a fault-injected copy
Method: simulation - no fault-injection harness for fs in this package; the instrument is S
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: packages/audio/src/cache.ts copyToFixtures: `copyFileSync(src.audioPath, dst.audioPath); copyFileSync(src.metaPath, dst.metaPath);` vs atomicWrite for the cache dir

instrument: owner decision: destination vocabulary; then a schemas test pinning the new fields
title: Rights record lacks the account, terms date and cleared destination
body:
## Summary
The audio asset record keeps plan tier, model, request and prompt hash, but not which account generated it, the terms in force, or the destination it is cleared for.

## Description
packages/schemas AudioAssetSchema (via packages/audio/src/generate.ts DraftAudioAsset) and the cache record (packages/audio/src/cache.ts CacheMeta) carry no account identity or destination. Registry: generated-music-acceptance rights-and-provenance-record lists account + plan tier, vendor/model/version + date, brief, reference material, and the intended destination as the per-asset record. Adding them is a schema + DB + policy change whose vocabulary (what a 'destination' is for StatReel) is the owner's.

## Flow
- define the destination vocabulary (e.g. youtube-shorts private draft)
- record account identity at generation (free subscription/user call)
- publish gate reads destination vs target

## Expected impact
A take can be re-cleared against its record when a channel changes; today only the tier is evidenced.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the rights record holds what clearance needs
Before: 2 of 5 technique fields recorded (tier, brief hash)
After: 5 of 5 once defined
Method: simulation - fields enumerated against the technique; not measurable until the owner defines the destination vocabulary
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence: packages/audio/src/generate.ts asset fields: kind, provider, request_id, model_id, voice_id|prompt_sha256, generated_at, sha256, c2pa, plan_tier
